# Seasonal menu planning

I plan menus around the seasonality of produce rather than around recipes. Asparagus has a short window in late spring; squash and chestnuts arrive in October. When a vegetable is ripe and abundant it is cheap and tastes best, so the calendar decides the menu and not the other way round.

A glut is both a gift and a problem. Twenty kilos of tomatoes in August need a plan: sauce, passata, a batch of roasted tomatoes in the freezer. I note on the calendar when each window opens and closes, then work backwards to decide what to preserve.

The shopping list follows the market. Out of season, I lean on pantry staples and the freezer.
